text:
Ben Kindel is 19, playing almost 18 minutes a night for a Penguins team that has lost eight of his last ten games, and the scoresheet hasn't been kind to him. He has 4 goals and 10 points in 20 games, and just four points in the last ten.

Most of the gap is bad luck. Pittsburgh has scored 11.3 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, one of the biggest shortfalls we track this season, and that has cost him assists in particular. His own chances add up to 5.6 expected goals against his four.

The honest concern is territory. At 5v5 the Penguins take 48% of the expected goals with him out there, about six points worse than without him, which is normal for a teenage center getting thrown into a top-nine role and not something to ignore either. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries last season, the habit you want from a young forward. Among forwards picked 6th to 16th since 2005, the median first full season was 0.37 points a game; he's at 0.50. The luck should turn before the territory does.
